transcript.question: What is something that Andrew could do to make birdwatching hobby to fit in his city schedule?

**Quick tip for fitting birdwatching into a city life:**

- **Turn your balcony or windowsill into a “mini‑feeder station.”**  
  • Hang a small feeder (e.g., sunflower‑seed or suet) on a balcony railing or a window frame.  
  • Use a lightweight, fold‑away bird‑watching chair or a small cushion so you can sit comfortably while you scan the sky.  
  • Keep a compact notebook or a note‑taking app (e.g., iNaturalist, eBird) handy to log sightings and use the new analytics tools at work to track patterns—this turns casual spotting into a data‑driven hobby.

- **Schedule “bird‑watching windows.”**  
  • Pick 15‑minute slots early in the morning (e.g., 5–6 am) or late afternoon (e.g., 4–5 pm) when city traffic is lighter and birds are active.  
  • Set a phone reminder so you don’t miss the window.

- **Leverage your work tools.**  
  • Use the analytics dashboards to log each sighting, noting time, species, and weather.  
  • Over time, you’ll see trends that can help you plan future trips (e.g., to Fox Hollow) or adjust your feeder setup.

By turning a small outdoor space into a dedicated bird‑watching spot and syncing it with your work analytics, Andrew can enjoy his hobby without needing a full‑time schedule change.
